unharnessed.meaning: Every fact survives: 28 years at the Bureau he founded, pneumonia, 73, "reform fanatic", prohibition and narcotics laws, Sunday amusements, the Dempsey-Carpentier fight, Westerly burial, Fryeburg, Wesleyan 1869, Boston 1871, the denominational moves, Sara J. Timanus, six lectures a week in twenty-nine countries, "Rhetoric Made Racy.", the Quarterly since 1896, the list of targets.
unharnessed.sense: Most terms fit: "barracking for prohibition", "his offsider", "sheer hard yakka", "Screen vamps", "ciggies". "heaps of his many goings-on" strains, as goings-on suggests shady doings, and "his gob" is cruder than "his voice" calls for.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian telling it: "that sort of carry-on", "had a red-hot go at stopping the Dempsey-Carpentier fight", "where he stayed put from then on". "The folks on his side" is more American.
unharnessed.register: Level-4 yarn throughout with dad-level swearing: "He wrote a bloody mountain of stuff on moral questions."
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the obituary's wry, measured respect mostly, but "His pen and his gob barely got a breather" and "goings-on" tip it a little toward mockery.
unharnessed.flow: Generally smooth, but the opening clause tangles: "who ran the International Reform Bureau he started himself for 28 years".
unharnessed.essence: Clearly the 1922 obituary of the reformer, in order, down to the "Rhetoric Made Racy" aside and the list of his targets.

engine.meaning: Mostly the original verbatim, but two facts are changed: the list of targets now reads "Sunday baseball, darts were a few of the objects" (cigarettes became darts), and the book title is altered to "Rhetoric Made Racy, ay."
engine.sense: Several insertions take the wrong sense or misfire: "darts" for cigarettes, "Bloody hell, in 1874 he married", "his bloody attacks on popular amusements", "carked it" in a death notice.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian interjections bolted onto untouched 1922 prose: "Crikey, WASHINGTON, Dec. 27.", "Well, he was 73 years old.", "Now, he was a prolific writer".
engine.register: The underlying text is untranslated ("By those in sympathy with his policies he was credited with having an influential part"), with swearing sprinkled on top; nowhere near a level-4 yarn.
engine.tone: The obituary is made flippant by "carked it at a hospital here today of pneumonia" and "Bloody hell, in 1874 he married Sara J. Timanus".
engine.flow: Jarring joins throughout: "Crikey, WASHINGTON, Dec. 27.—Dr. Wilbur F. Crafts", "Rhetoric Made Racy, ay."
engine.variety: A handful of tics: "Crikey", "Well,", "Now,", "Bloody hell", "bloody", "old man's", "ay".
engine.essence: Recognisably the obituary, but the inserted exclamations and the altered title and list distort it: "Rhetoric Made Racy, ay."

yarn.meaning: All facts kept, in order, from "for 28 years the boss of the International Reform Bureau, which he started himself" to the targets list. "how much he hated Sunday entertainment" is a touch stronger than "opposition", and Sara's "forceful" becomes "threw her weight behind religious causes".
yarn.sense: Every term fits: "best known as a wowser" is exactly the Australian word for his kind, "the mob who fought the laws he put up", "did his level best", "sheer hard yakka", "knocked out a book a year".
yarn.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian yarn-teller, idiom used the local way: "wowser", "had a red-hot go at getting it banned", "where he stayed for good".
yarn.register: Level-4 throughout, vulgarity at dad level: "his bloody tireless attacks on the things people did for fun".
yarn.tone: Keeps the obituary's wry respect: "a colourful sight in the lobbies and committee rooms of Congress", "Here's a funny one, for instance".
yarn.flow: Reads naturally: "He spent the first eight years of his long run as a minister in his old man's church, switched to Congregationalism in 1880".
yarn.variety: Varied ("boss", "mob", "reckoned", "red-hot go", "level best", "hard yakka", "wowser"), with one repeat: "He wrote a stack" and "turned out books by the stack".
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the obituary of the reformer, its wry close kept: "Sunday baseball, ciggies — they were a few of the targets of his reforming zeal."

unharnessed.quote: who was his offsider in heaps of his many goings-on
unharnessed.original: his partner in many of his numerous activities
unharnessed.why: "Goings-on" implies shady doings; "heaps of his many" also doubles up.

unharnessed.quote: His pen and his gob barely got a breather
unharnessed.original: His pen and his voice were allowed little rest
unharnessed.why: "Gob" is a touch crude for an obituary.

unharnessed.quote: who ran the International Reform Bureau he started himself for 28 years
unharnessed.original: for 28 years superintendent of the International Reform Bureau which he founded
unharnessed.why: Clause order makes it read as if he started it for 28 years.

engine.quote: Sunday baseball, darts were a few of the objects
engine.original: Sunday baseball, cigarettes were a few of the objects
engine.why: Cigarettes became darts; a reader would think he campaigned against the game.

engine.quote: Bloody hell, in 1874 he married Sara J. Timanus
engine.original: In 1874 he married Sara J. Timanus
engine.why: Senseless exclamation that mocks the marriage.

engine.quote: carked it at a hospital here today of pneumonia
engine.original: died at a hospital here today of pneumonia
engine.why: Flippant slang for death inside formal obituary prose.

engine.quote: By those in sympathy with his policies he was credited with having an influential part
engine.original: By those in sympathy with his policies he was credited with having an influential part
engine.why: Representative: the body is left untranslated.

yarn.quote: who turned out books by the stack herself
yarn.why: Repeats "stack" from a few lines earlier.

yarn.quote: how much he hated Sunday entertainment
yarn.original: Outspoken in his opposition to Sunday amusements
yarn.why: "Hated" is stronger than the original's opposition.

summaries.unharnessed: A lively, accurate level-4 retelling with good Australian idiom; a few word choices tip the obituary toward mockery.
summaries.engine: The original with stagey interjections and swearing bolted on, a changed fact and an altered title; broken tone and flow.
summaries.yarn: An excellent level-4 retelling, accurate and natural, with "wowser" landing perfectly; the best of the three.
